Yes—several papers address medical knowledge graphs for clinical LLMs. One focuses on how to integrate biomedical KGs into LLMs for clinical diagnosis, finding that KG-judgment training with KL regularization gives sparse “surgical alignment” updates and can improve reasoning quality [1]. Another builds multimodal patient knowledge graphs with explicit alignment edges so clinical LLMs can link patient evidence to biomedical knowledge, making retrieval traceable and testable [2].

Other papers are more specific: one studies when KG grounding helps clinical QA and finds it mainly helps for out-of-training or novel facts, not public KG facts [3]. Another proposes a biomedical KG with temporal grounding for clinical reasoning and retrieval-augmented systems [6], and another evaluates GraphRAG plus continual pretraining from UMLS for biomedical language models and LLaMA [9].
